findings.section: A second Region protects against Region failure but replicates asynchronously
findings.quote: 3. **The copy runs behind.** AWS [does not provide a synchronous Cross-Region replication feature](../facts/global-infrastructure.md#global-infrastructure-no-synchronous-cross-region-replication).
findings.evidence: Saved AWS page docs/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/HowItWorks.ReadConsistency (fetched 2026-10-09): "With multi-Region strong consistency (MRSC), item changes are synchronously replicated to another Region before the write returns, and strongly consistent read operations on any replica always return the latest version of an item." The fact global-infrastructure-no-synchronous-cross-region-replication quotes a fault-isolation whitepaper whose sentence ends "at this time" ("AWS does not provide a synchronous Cross-Region replication feature at this time."); the display drops that qualifier and the chapter states it as a timeless rule. Same claim in: 1-fast.md Choose it or not row "Synchronous copies? ... No: AWS has no [synchronous Cross-Region replication feature]"; the heading "A second Region protects against Region failure but replicates asynchronously"; the table row "| Survive a Region failure | A second Region | Asynchronous |"; the Exam trap "AWS offers no "synchronous replica in another Region"."; the Say it "The thing to watch is that the copy runs behind." She works at AWS and would tell a founder something a DynamoDB global table with MRSC disproves.
findings.suggestion: Teach the rule as the general case with its named exception: most cross-Region replication (S3 CRR, Aurora Global Database, DynamoDB global tables in the default MREC mode) is asynchronous; DynamoDB global tables can be set to multi-Region strong consistency. Request a fact from the DynamoDB page, re-scope or retire the whitepaper fact, keep the heading true ("... usually replicates asynchronously"), and add a Changed recently entry if MRSC is newer than mid-2022.
findings.resolution: fix-02: the absolute is gone from step 3, the plain table, the trap and the Say it (async fact; 'Services differ.'); the whitepaper fact was rejected. The MRSC exception and a Changed recently entry need a verified DynamoDB fact (chapter 28), not in the canon yet. The heading is a brief section id (L905); the orchestrator can rename it in brief.json.

findings.section: Question 7 (aws-map-q009); also data/02-aws-map/cards.json aws-map-c007 and data/02-aws-map/speak.json aws-map-s02
findings.quote: **Twin.** If the stem said "a Region failure must lose no committed write" instead: no AWS replication feature meets it, because AWS [does not provide a synchronous Cross-Region replication feature](../facts/global-infrastructure.md#global-infrastructure-no-synchronous-cross-region-replication).
findings.evidence: Saved AWS page docs/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/HowItWorks.ReadConsistency: "With multi-Region strong consistency (MRSC), item changes are synchronously replicated to another Region before the write returns". The twin line states that no AWS feature meets a zero-loss Region failover; for a DynamoDB table one does. The same absolute appears in card aws-map-c007 ("can you replicate data synchronously from one Region to another Region?" => "No. Replication between Regions is asynchronous."), in speak aws-map-s02 ten_second ("expect asynchronous copies"), key point kp4 and must_not_say 2 ("AWS does not provide a synchronous cross-Region replication feature"), and in the Q7 why-not line for the synchronous-replica option ("so this replica cannot be built with an AWS feature"). Q7 itself names a "managed relational database", so its key can stay; the twin, the why-not wording, the card and the speak item generalize past it.
findings.suggestion: Scope each item to the service: Q7 why-not and twin to relational databases (or name the service), card c007 to a decide or differ card that names DynamoDB MRSC as the exception or retire it, speak s02 kp4 to "most cross-Region copies are asynchronous" with a follow-up that names the exception.
findings.resolution: fix-02: q009 rewritten and reset (twin and why-not no longer claim impossibility; the cross-Region synchronous option is replaced); card c007 is now a differ card on the async fact; speak s02 kp4, must_not_say 2 and the ten-second answer are scoped to asynchronous copies.

findings.section: Each request goes to one Region and your resources stay there
findings.quote: 1. **Choose the Region.** Some services, such as IAM, need none: [IAM resources are global](../facts/iam.md#iam-resources-global-same-role-any-region).
findings.evidence: The chapter never explains the three scopes that the AWS map is about: global, Regional and zonal. The words appear without a definition: "Regional services" (1-fast.md Choose it or not and Signals tables), "IAM resources are global" here, "Regional service such as Amazon S3" (hero figure step 4), and "An EC2 instance is a zonal resource" in the Question 4 explanation. The heading "Each request goes to one Region" is then false for the global service named in step 1. Rule STYLE 2 (five term steps) and STYLE 11.10 (headings survive the skim). Without the scope idea she cannot reason through an unseen question such as "which resources must I recreate in the second Region".
findings.suggestion: Add a 3-row truth table (scope | example | what fails with it): zonal (EC2 instance, subnet, EBS volume) | Regional (S3 bucket, DynamoDB table) | global (IAM role, CloudFront distribution). Heading: "A Regional resource lives in one Region and AWS copies it nowhere".
findings.resolution: fix-02: subsection 1 now says 'Services come in three scopes, [zonal, Regional, and global](global-infrastructure-three-service-types-zonal-regional-global): an EC2 instance, an S3 bucket, an IAM role.' Its Stop and answer now asks which of an IAM role and a DynamoDB table works from another Region. A 3-row table and a heading change were not made: the deep file is at its 2,400-word cap and the heading is a brief section id.

findings.section: A second Region protects against Region failure but replicates asynchronously (Go deeper: static stability)
findings.quote: [Deploying new instances through auto scaling relies on the EC2 control plane](../facts/global-infrastructure.md#global-infrastructure-auto-scaling-relies-on-ec2-control-plane). Spare capacity that already runs gives [static stability](../facts/global-infrastructure.md#global-infrastructure-static-stability-definition).
findings.evidence: Mechanism stated without cause and effect: "control plane" and "static stability" are not defined, and the text never says why relying on the control plane is a risk (launches take time and depend on a service that can be impaired during the same event). Question 9 (aws-map-q012) is decided by this idea, and its Review link points to this subsection. The B-list row "| [50% additional instances] | Static stability, three AZs |" gives a number with no explanation of where 50% comes from (six needed, nine run: three extra). STYLE 10.2: can she redraw the causal chain from it?
findings.suggestion: Three numbered steps: one zone fails; new instances must be launched by the EC2 control plane and take time; so capacity that already runs in the other zones keeps the service up. Then the 6 to 9 arithmetic as the worked case.
findings.resolution: fix-02: the static stability Go deeper (now in the AZ subsection) gives the chain: after a zone fails, deploying new instances relies on the EC2 control plane and takes time, so pre-provisioned capacity gives static stability. The 6-to-9 arithmetic stays in the B-list row and the q012 explanation (word cap).

findings.section: The best Region is near your users and meets your data rules
findings.quote: Why? Moving data between places costs money: [keep your data close to your customer and close to the resources](../facts/well-architected.md#well-architected-data-transfer-cost-keep-data-close).
findings.evidence: The Why reason answers a different question (data transfer cost) from the heading claim (near users, inside the law). The cause of the latency rule (distance adds network latency) is never stated as cause and effect. CONVENTIONS-2 U1 / STYLE 11.1: one "Why does AWS work this way?" reason, said as a customer would hear it. The subsection is also below its length range (lint W201: 145 words; a subsection needs 150 to 400), so there is room.
findings.suggestion: Why? "Every request travels to the Region and back. The farther the Region, the longer each trip." Keep the data-transfer point as a fifth checklist item or a Go deeper.
findings.resolution: fix-02: Why line now 'Why? The farther the Region, the longer each request travels.' The data-transfer clause was removed.

findings.section: The best Region is near your users and meets your data rules
findings.quote: 4. **Price.** AWS says to [only deploy in Regions with higher costs to meet latency, data residency and data sovereignty requirements](../facts/well-architected.md#well-architected-region-pricing-differs-choose-by-cost).

The intended rule (pay a higher Region price only when latency or data rules require it) is not said in plain words outside the quote. findings.resolution: fix-02: step 4 now 'If a cheaper Region meets your rules, use it: [only deploy in Regions with higher costs to meet latency, data residency and data sovereignty requirements].' The plain rule comes first.

Check 2 (DynamoDB IAM permissions) repeats Predict 2 and Trap 2, and the deep shared-responsibility Stop and answer asks the same DynamoDB case again ("A team moves its job records from an EC2 database to Amazon DynamoDB"). The deep Stop and answer "A news site serves the same images ... to readers on five continents" is answered by the table row "| Content near users worldwide | Edge locations |" and the fast Signals row. The endpoint Stop and answer (us-east-1 table, us-west-2 endpoint) is answered by the heading "Each request goes to one Region and your resources stay there". Four of nine prompts fall to the skim.

The edge-location Stop and answer was kept (deep file at word cap).

findings.section: AWS secures the cloud and you secure what you put in it
findings.quote: **Spot the bug.** A startup's notes say: "Amazon S3 is managed, so AWS controls who reads our objects. We patch our EC2 instance." What is wrong?
findings.evidence: STYLE 11.7: Spot the bug is not obvious. The bug is the exact sentence of 1-fast.md Trap 2 ("**Wrong belief:** On Amazon S3, AWS decides who reads the data.") and of the item 3 heading just above ("On Amazon S3, data and access: you."). She finds it by matching words, not by reasoning; this is her weakest domain (Secure 45%).
findings.suggestion: Use a less visible split: "We use Amazon RDS, so AWS patches the database engine and also chooses whether the snapshots are encrypted", or a security group on EC2 left to AWS.
findings.resolution: fix-02: Spot the bug now reads 'On Amazon EC2 we patch the guest operating system, and AWS configures our security groups.' The answer links the customer's configuration of the security group firewall. The bug is no longer a copy of a trap or heading.

Same in 2-services.md: "The CLI guide lists the access keys of an IAM user as [(Not recommended) Use long-term credentials, which have no expiration]", where a bracketed label and a capital imperative sit inside the sentence.
findings.suggestion: Use a shorter verbatim display that starts lower case, or put the quote after a colon.
findings.resolution: fix-02: deep Why line is now 'Business needs differ.
